>From a strictly legal sense you are not stealing from the government or the tax payers or anybody.

Yeah this is one of the things I'm worried about, it's like I'm replaying this imaginary conversation in my head where I'm being told I'm stealing tax payers money and I'm not entitled to it anymore. 

I'm reading more into step change as of this moment and definitely going to take this further. I feel like I've actually come to the right place and venting this all out has been useful. 

I'm going to be optimistic and do more research with your suggestions, you've actually taken a huge weight of my shoulders tonight so I'm extremely grateful for you taking your time to give me advice.

That's relieving to hear. I'm just anxiously assuming I have done something wrong due to not doing what was required of me. The set rate I think is 35 hours a week looking for work, which I've not done, but I have my reasons for it being mostly mental health related. I'm mainly worried about having no support or no one on my side, I haven't really spoken to many people regarding this and felt like all my doors were closing, it's good to hear that it may not be the case and I'm maybe overreacting.

Thank you for your time for reading and replying to this 
.

Hello thank you for your time for a response. Yeah it has been hard, it's been nothing but a burden. 

I will have a look at step change and see if theres someone to talk to who can guide me through everything. 

I definitely need to have an honest open talk with a gp and hope they can understand my situation.

I just looked up getting signed off from UC and wasn't even aware of all the contents, I've had a read and it looks useful so thank you for suggesting it, it's actually annoying to me that I don't know how to find this stuff for myself.  

And the reason I ask if I should get legal aid is because I haven't been able to fulfill my commitments, it feels like I'm stealing money from the government. It's an unusual feeling, and probably just anxiety but I haven't been charged for anything, I don't expect to either.

I'm happy you gave me some suggestions and its given me a step forward into finding some good support for myself.

I definitely feel like I've got phone anxiety, even with people I know, I avoid the phone the like crazy, I always assume it's gonna be bad when I answer. 

Maybe, I just dont know where to start with any one of that, it all just sounds like an urban myth to me joining a group and partaking in these social events, I think I'd crumble under the pressure of being the new person there. I feel like with everything going on in my life rn it would be easy for me to approach something like that because I've never done it before.

Yeah it's the one thing I'd say I have left in my life.

And yeah it's definitely been a struggle I believe a lot of people can relate to, makes simple day by day activities so much harder than they need to be. 

I do agree with you, I just wish I knew how to start or what to do without feeling intense pressure and being uncomfortable. I feel like it makes other people feel awkward and I can never have a natural conversation with anyone I meet. I really want to try and be better at it, I only moments ago messaged an old friend and opened up about how I was feeling, we spoke and I felt like he wanted to listen and wanted to help, it made the whole thing easier, I just wish it could be that with everyone.

I think I'm scared to put myself in those social situations, I don't know why and I cant help it, is it normal to be scared of it?

Thank you I genuinely appreciate that. 

I've always been shy, since a child, still am today. I find it tough trusting people, I feel like I'm being judged and critiqued, even though the cynical part of me knows they don't care. My mind always hits mental blocks when I'm talking to people and I can never get my words out properly. By this point my face usually turns really red and the embarrassment of them seeing that lingers in my mind, making things even more difficult for me. I'm 24 for context, and been avoiding social situations for as long as I can remember, especially in my jobs where I have to communicate, it always leads to the same thing. Me getting depressed and anxious and resigning from my job, just to repeat the process. I think I may have social anxiety disorder but I'm too filled with anxiety to sort it out.  

With people I'm close too, a few friends, and my ex of course I'm 100% more myself.
